NOTES
Virtual Meeting
1. In continuation of the framework prescribed by the Ministry 
of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) vide general circular nos. 
14/2020 dated April 8, 2020, 17/2020 dated April 13, 2020, 
20/2020 dated May 5, 2020 and subsequent circulars 
issued in this regard latest being 09/2024 dated September 
19, 2024, SEBI vide circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/
CIR/2024/133 dated October 3, 2024 (hereinafter collectively 
referred to as “Circulars”), have permitted the holding of the 
annual general meeting (“AGM”) through video conference 
(“VC”) / other audio-visual means (“OAVM”), without physical 
presence of members at a common venue. Accordingly, in 
compliance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 
(“Act”) read with the Circulars, the 24th AGM of the Company 
is being conducted through VC/ OAVM. 
2. The 24th AGM shall be deemed to be held at the registered 
office of the Company i.e., 401, 4th Floor, Man Excellenza, S.V. 
Road, Vile Parle (West), Mumbai - 400 056, Maharashtra, 
India as prescribed under the Circulars.
3. Since, the 24th AGM is being conducted through VC/ OAVM 
pursuant to the Circulars, requirement of physical attendance 
of members have been dispensed with. Accordingly, the 
facility for appointment of proxies by members is not available 
for the 24th AGM and hence proxy form and attendance slip 
including route map has not been annexed with the notice of 
the 24th AGM (“Notice”).
4. Members attending the 24th AGM through VC/ OAVM 
including authorized representative(s)/ attorney holder(s) 
of corporate members, institutional investors etc. shall be 
counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum under the 
provisions of section 103 of the Act.

 (ii) Deduction of Tax at Source (“TDS”) on Dividend
  a. Pursuant to the changes introduced by the Finance 
Act 2020, w.e.f. April 1, 2020 in relation to taxation 
of dividend, Dividend Distribution Tax which used 
to be payable by the Company is abolished, and 
instead, the members are liable to pay tax on the 
dividend income. Accordingly, the Company, in 
compliance with the provisions of the Income Tax 
Act, 1961 (“IT Act”), would be required to deduct 
tax at source (“TDS”) at the prescribed rates on 
the dividend paid to its members. TDS rate would 
vary depending on the residential status of the 
member and the documents submitted by them 
and accepted by the Company.
  b. The Company has sent detailed communication 
in this regard to all members on Tuesday, June 
24, 2025, informing the relevant procedure 
to be adopted by them and documents to be 
submitted for availing exemption/ the applicable 
tax rate. The said communication, exemption 
forms and other documents, are available 
on the website of the Company viz. https://
www.maxhealthcare.in/investors/shareholder-
information/investor-downloads. The documents 
for availing exemption/ applicable tax rate needs 
to be submitted by following procedure latest by 
Thursday, July 10, 2025.   c. In the event the benefit of lower tax on dividend 
cannot be provided by the Company due to 
non-receipt/ late receipt of the tax exemption 
forms or the forms & documents, members will 
still have an option to claim appropriate refund, 
if eligible, at the time of filing their income tax 
returns. No claim shall lie against the Company 
for taxes once deducted.
 (iii) Unclaimed/ Unpaid Dividend and transfer to Investor 
Education and Protection Fund
  In terms of provisions of section 124 of the Act and 
rules made thereunder, the dividend that remain 
unclaimed/ unpaid for a period of 7 (seven) years from 
the date of transfer to the Company’s Unpaid Dividend 
Account, will be transferred to the Investor Education 
and Protection Fund (“IEPF”). Further, all shares in 
respect of which dividends have remained unclaimed 
for 7 (Seven) consecutive years or more are required 
to be transferred to IEPF. Once unclaimed/ unpaid 
dividend or shares are transferred to IEPF, no claim 
shall lie in respect thereof with the Company. In view 
of this, Members are requested to claim their dividend 
from the Company, within the stipulated timeline. 
  Members may note that the Company had declared 
dividend for financial year 2022-23 and financial year 
2023-24. As a period of 7 (Seven) years have not elapsed 
from the date of transfer of the said dividend amounts 
to the respective Unpaid Dividend Accounts, the 
provisions relating to the transfer of unpaid/ unclaimed 
dividend to the IEPF are currently not applicable to the 
Company, hence there was no amount to be transferred 
to IEPF during the financial year 2024-25.
  Members wishing to claim unclaimed dividends 
are requested to correspond with RTA at  
delhi@in.mpms.mufg.com or the Company Secretary 
at investors@maxhealthcare.com. Further, pursuant to 
section 124(2) of the Act, the Company has uploaded 
details of unpaid and unclaimed dividend amount 
lying as on Saturday, May 31, 2025 with the Company 
in respect of dividend declared for the financial year 
2022-23 and 2023-24, on the website of the Company 
viz. https://www.maxhealthcare.in/investors/dividends.

11. Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Mechanism
 a. SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/ 
CIR/2023/131 dated July 31, 2023, as updated from 
time to time, has established a common Online Dispute 
Resolution Portal (“ODR Portal”) for resolution of 
disputes arising in the Indian Securities Market.
 b. Pursuant to above Circular, a member shall first take 
up his/ her grievance with the Company by lodging 
a complaint directly with the Company/ RTA and 
if the grievance is not redressed satisfactorily, the 
member may escalate the same through existing 
SCORES Portal. Post exhausting all available options 
for resolution of the grievance, if the member is 
still not satisfied with the outcome, he/ she can 
initiate dispute resolution through the ODR Portal at  
https://smartodr.in/login.

the stock exchanges the details of the agreements entered

promoter(s) group, related parties, directors, key managerial 
personnel, employees of the Company or of its holding, 
subsidiary or associate company, among themselves or with 
the Company or with a third party, solely or jointly, which,

and effect is to, impact the management or control of the 
Company or impose any restriction or create any liability 
upon the Company, including disclosure of any rescission, 
amendment or alteration of such agreements thereto, 
whether or not the Company is a party to such agreements.
 Accordingly, it is hereby advised to the members to inform 
the Company about such agreement to which the Company 
is not a party, within two working days of entering into such 
agreements or signing an agreement to enter into such 
agreements. The Company will inform the details of such 
agreements to the stock exchanges on it becoming aware of 
it within the prescribed timelines.
 [Explanation: The term “directly or indirectly” includes

Brief profile of Mr Anil Kumar Bhatnagar
Mr Anil Kumar Bhatnagar has rich experience of over 4 (four) 
decades in corporate and commercial litigation including 
international and domestic arbitrations. He is a former Senior 
Partner of one of the top legal firm, Dua Associates. He has handled 
a large number of domestic arbitrations covering corporate and 
commercial disputes arising out of joint ventures, Government and 
private contracts, civil construction and engineering contracts.
He has conducted International Arbitration in several countries 
including proceedings before Arbitral Tribunals constituted by the 
International Chamber of Commerce, Paris and London Court of 
International Arbitration, London.
As a litigator, he has regularly appeared as Counsel in a large 
number of matters before the Supreme Court of India, Delhi High 
Court, other state High Courts and Statutory Tribunals. He holds a 
Bachelor’s degree in Science from the University of Delhi and also 
a Bachelor of Laws degree from the Faculty of Law, University of 
Delhi. He is enrolled with the Delhi Bar Council.
The profile of Mr Bhatnagar can also be accessed on the 
Company’s website at https://www.maxhealthcare.in/leadership/
anil-bhatnagar .
Proposal, rationale and justification for continuation of  
Mr Anil Kumar Bhatnagar as Non-Executive 
Non-Independent Director
The Company follows a robust process for appointment,  
re-appointment and continuation of Board members. NRC oversees 
the succession planning, inter-alia, for the Board and thoroughly 
assesses various factors including health, age, background, 
expertise, skill set, experience, performance evaluation, 
educational & professional qualifications, personal achievements.
Further, the Board also deliberates on various factors including 
composition of the Board to ensure optimum combination of 
executive and non-executive directors, tenure of the Board 
members, skill matrix, board diversity, time-commitment and 
statutory requirements. 
In line with the above, NRC, at its meetings held on  
March 11, 2025 and May 19, 2025, inter-alia, reviewed succession 
planning framework and evaluated tenure of directors, 
including tenure of Mr Bhatnagar who will attain the age of 75 
(seventy-five) years in August 2025. Post due deliberation, NRC 
considered and recommended the proposal for continuation of 
Mr Bhatnagar as a Non-Executive Non-Independent Director on 
the Company’s Board.
As evident from the information provided above, Mr Bhatnagar 
has maintained a perfect 100% attendance record at Board and 
Committee meetings since his appointment as a Non-Executive 
Non-Independent Director. His unwavering dedication and 
commitment to Company's mission is commendable.
Mr Bhatnagar’s active participation in all Board and Committee 
meetings is a testament to his deep engagement with the 
Company’s affairs. He consistently leverages his expertise,  
inter-alia, in corporate and commercial litigation, including 
international and domestic arbitrations for meaningful discussions at the Board and he provides valuable mentorship to Company’s 
management team. His prompt attention to requests from 
Company’s management underscores his devotion to the 
Company’s long-term mission.
NRC, after taking into account the positive outcome of the 
performance evaluation of Mr Bhatnagar during his current term 
as Non-Executive Non-Independent Director and considering 
his skills, business acumen, knowledge, time commitment to the 
Company, rich and varied experience as well as his significant 
contribution to the Company’s evolution as an industry leader 
and one of India’s largest healthcare providers, recommended 
his continuation as Non-Executive Non-Independent Director 
on the Board, beyond the age of 75 (seventy-five) years, till the 
completion of his current tenure i.e., September 30, 2026. NRC 
further noted that skills, expertise and competencies possessed 
by Mr Bhatnagar are in alignment with the skills and expertise 
identified by NRC and the Board, for the Directors of the Company.
The Board, at its meeting held on May 20, 2025, considered 
the recommendation of NRC along with the comprehensive 
performance evaluation report of Mr Bhatnagar. The Board duly 
recognized Mr Bhatnagar’s remarkable skills, deep understanding, 
business transformation, compliance and assurance. In view of 
his sustained contribution as a Non-Executive Non-Independent 
Director over the years, the Board believes that Mr Bhatnagar’s 
continued association as Non-Executive Non-Independent 
Director would be of immense benefit to the Company during this 
pivotal phase of growth. 
Performance Evaluation
The Board, in consultation with NRC, had formulated a framework 
containing the criteria for performance evaluation of the entire 
Board, its Committees, Chairman and Individual Directors. 
NRC and Board while considering performance evaluation of  
Mr Bhatnagar, inter-alia, considered his valuable guidance in risk 
mitigation, assessment of his judgement that contributes to Board’s 
deliberations, strategy and performance, his understanding of 
Company’s business and goals, confidentiality, adherence to 
legal obligations and Company’s code of conduct along with his 
understanding of roles and responsibilities as a Non-Executive 
Non-Independent Director. 
NRC and the Board are of the opinion that Mr Bhatnagar 
possesses relevant expertise and experience and duly 
fulfils the conditions specified in the Act, rules made there 
under and SEBI Listing Regulations for his continuation as a  
Non-Executive Non-Independent Director on the Board 
of the Company.

to bring world-class healthcare to communities and redefine 
patient care. Today, as we mark this significant milestone, we 
look back at the challenges, the breakthroughs and the lives 
transformed. This edition of our annual report tells the story of 
that journey and our plans for the future.
It is incredible to think that what started 
as a vision for exceptional care has 
grown into India’s most valuable listed 
healthcare organisation. Today, with 22 
healthcare facilities, over 5,100 beds and 
a dedicated team of more than 35,000 
individuals, Max Healthcare is making a 
difference in 651 cities across India and 
183 countries worldwide. In FY 25 alone, 
we treated ~35 Lakh patients. Every life 
touched testifies to our commitment to 
compassionate, world-class healthcare. 
The ever-expanding MHC family, 
which includes our growing network of 
hospitals, healthcare professionals, and 
partners, continues to play a vital role in 
realising our mission. We have been on a 
robust growth trajectory, with FY 2025–
26 set to accelerate our expansion. 
Staying true to our commitment to 
enhancing access to high-quality medical 
care, we are advancing on multiple 
fronts, i.e., developing a greenfield 
hospital in Sector 56, Gurugram 
and executing significant brownfield 
expansions across Mohali, Mumbai, Saket 
and Patparganj. Our newly acquired 
hospitals in Lucknow, Nagpur, Noida 
and Bulandshahr will further strengthen 
our network, ensuring better access to 
world-class healthcare across India. We 
are also planning to add over 3,900 new 
beds in the next 3-4 years through our 
greenfield and brownfield expansions, 
enabling us to serve more communities 
and meet the growing demand for 
advanced healthcare.
We continue to earn recognition for our

commitment to fostering an environment 
where employees thrive, feel valued, 
and are empowered to succeed. This 
recognition, grounded in the feedback

and collaboration we continually strive to 
nurture. At Max Healthcare, every voice 
matters, every perspective adds value, 
and every individual plays a pivotal role 
in the story we continue to write.
At Max Healthcare, our responsibility 
extends beyond clinical care. Through 
impactful CSR initiatives, we strive to 
empower communities and uplift lives.

funded the medical education of 144 
meritorious students, strengthening 
the future of healthcare. In FY 25, we

medical treatment to 3,47,000 patients to 
ensure that financial barriers never stood 
in the way of quality medical care.
Innovation has been central to Max

robotic systems to using cutting-edge

for precision cancer care, we are 
reshaping possibilities in healthcare.

About the Report
Max Healthcare Institute Limited (hereafter referred to as ‘Max Healthcare’, and ‘The 
Company’) has been delivering compassionate care and clinical excellence for ~25 years while balancing business growth with environmental and social responsibilities.
The Company is pleased to present its second Integrated Annual Report ("Report"), which provides holistic disclosures of its 
financial and non-financial performance for the Financial Year ("FY") 2024–25. The report shares details of how Max Healthcare is shaping its strategic direction in consultation with stakeholders to address their most critical concerns and expectations in line with sustainable principles and sound governance practices.

into their recovery journey while helping 
reduce avoidable readmissions.

enabling a smarter, more responsive 
healthcare system—one that is predictive, 
personalised, and centred around the 
patient at every step.

behaviour-driven CRM campaigns across

complemented by speciality-specific and 
seasonal communication based on user 
behaviour analytics.

true business impact of these platforms. 
We also initiated new aggregator 
partnerships in select hospitals, with 
plans underway to scale this approach 
across our network.

MIME and MIAPE, our academic arms, 
offering immersive, cross-disciplinary 
learning programmes.
In FY 25, our academic and research 
ecosystem grew in both scale and 
influence. Over 2,800 clinical research 
publications were authored by our 
clinicians, while 650+ active research 
projects and grants reflected our 
leadership in evidence-based medicine.Our academic platform now includes 
270+ structured courses, 1,570+ faculty 
members, and has trained over 1.2 
Lakh students in medical education and 
3,500 students in allied and paramedical 
disciplines. Collaborations with leading 
global institutions such as Imperial 
College London, Deakin University, 
and Ashoka University continue to 
strengthen our research focus areas 
in oncology, genomics, diabetes, and 
cardiovascular care.
Our flagship publication, the Max Medical 
Journal, now in its second year, continues 
to contribute to clinical knowledge and 
establish Max Healthcare as a thought 
leader in global healthcare discourse.
ESG, CSR and Awareneness 
Initiatives: Our 
Responsibility Beyond Business
As Max Healthcare continues to grow, 
we remain deeply mindful of our 
responsibility—not just to our patients and 
stakeholders, but to the environment, to 
society, and to future generations. Our 
Environmental, Social and Governance 
(ESG) agenda is not a parallel effort; 
it is woven into our core strategy and 
operational decisions, guiding us towards 
building a healthcare institution that 
is not only high-performing but also 
deeply responsible.
On the environmental front, we made 
meaningful progress this year in energy 
and resource conservation. Across 
our facilities, we consumed over 15.62 
million kWh of electricity from renewable 
sources, reflecting our commitment to 
clean energy adoption. We also achieved 
measurable reductions in both energy 
and waste intensity per occupied bed day, 
further enhancing operational efficiency 
and sustainability. As part of our water 
stewardship efforts, we rejuvenated three 
ponds to support groundwater recharge—
including a landmark project in Rajpura, 
Meerut, developed in collaboration with 
IIT Delhi. All our hospitals operate in line 
with ISO 14001 environmental standards, 
and our newer facilities are designed to 
align with IGBC Green Building principles, 
ensuring sustainability is built into 
their very foundations.
Our social responsibility efforts 
remained robust and deeply rooted in the communities we serve. Through our 
Max Medical Scholarship Programme, 
in its second year, we awarded 100 full 
scholarships to talented students from 
underserved backgrounds, enabling 
them to pursue careers in healthcare and 
become a part of India’s next generation 
of medical professionals. 
To create awareness about key healthcare 
issues, we did large format engagements 
on World Heart Day, World Cancer Day 
and during Breast Cancer Awareness 
Month in October 2024. Over 1.66 Lakh+ 
people enthusiastically participated in 
these and several other such activities.
Through every initiative—whether 
environmental conservation, health 
awareness, education, or rehabilitation—
our ESG vision remains clear: to build a 
healthier world not only within hospital 
walls, but far beyond them.
Financial Highlights
The financial performance in FY 2024–25 
stands as a strong validation of our 
strategic direction and operational 
resilience, highlighted by robust growth 
across key financial metrics. Our network 
gross revenue reached H9,065 Crore, 
reflecting a 26% year-on-year increase, 
while our operating EBITDA rose by 21.6% 
to H2,319 Crore. We also recorded a 
Profit After Tax of H1,392 Crore, excluding 
one time exceptional cost and gain of 
non-recurring nature—underscoring 
the strength of our financial foundation. 
Notably, several of our core indicators—
including ARPOB, EBITDA margins, 
and EBITDA per bed—achieved their 
highest-ever levels, continuing to lead the 
industry. This exceptional performance 
was driven by a greater share of complex 
quaternary care, widespread adoption of 
advanced medical technologies across 
our network, improved occupancy 
rates, and higher average revenue 
per occupied bed day.
Looking Ahead: The Next Chapter
As we step into the next phase of our 
journey, our ambition is clear. We intend 
to double our bed capacity over the 
next five years, enhance our digital and 
AI capabilities, and further deepen our 
clinical programmes in areas such as 
oncology, neurosciences, transplant medicine, and genomics. We will continue 
to drive ESG outcomes, invest in people, 
and build collaborative ecosystems that 
can solve healthcare’s biggest challenges.
We are confident that the platform we’ve 
built—strong in clinical depth, agile in 
execution, and guided by purpose—
positions us well to lead the next era of 
healthcare in India and beyond.
On this landmark occasion of 25 years 
of Max Healthcare, I extend my heartfelt 
gratitude to every individual who has 
been part of this journey—our patients, 
employees, partners, shareholders, and 
community members. Your trust and 
support have shaped Max Healthcare 
into what it is today.
Driven by purpose and an unwavering 
commitment to excellence, we look ahead 
with confidence—To serve. To excel.

Clinical Risks • Adverse outcomes or fatalities arising 
during clinical trials or the use of 
experimental treatments
• Incidents of medical negligence due to lapses 
in delivering high-quality care
• Harm to patients in the hospital, including 
diagnostic inaccuracies or reporting errors• Enforcement of rigorous protocols, including 
pre-feasibility assessments, adherence to safety 
guidelines and continuous staff training
• Implementation of clinical decision support systems, 
regular mortality and morbidity review meetings and 
comprehensive infection control training
• Adoption of international patient safety standards, 
supported by regular audits to ensure compliance 
and continuous improvement
• Continuous training of paramedical and non-medical staff
Financial Risks • Potential for fraud or data breaches in sensitive 
areas, such as front office, operation theatres 
(OT) and cath labs, due to manual controls 
• Lack of liquidity due to insufficient monitoring 
of receivables, weak credit risk management 
and use of short term borrowing for 
long term purpose.• Implementation of solutions to streamline billing, 
collections and customer payment processes 
including KYC linked validations to enhance 
transparency and enforce controls
• To mitigate liquidity and credit risk, the Group 
maintains adequate cash reserves which are 
invested in callable fixed deposits, enforce system-
based credit limits, monitors cash flows and aligns 
asset-liability maturities
Strategic Risks • A significant portion of the Network's revenue is 
concentrated in the NCR region, exposing the 
Group to potential disruptions arising from local 
economic conditions, regulatory changes or 
natural disasters 
• Risk of missing potential growth opportunities 
due to failure in identifying, securing or 
executing expansion initiatives • Diversification of business operations to reduce 
reliance on a single geographic region e.g. 
expanding of operations to Nagpur and Lucknow in 
FY 2023-24 and executing agreements for setting up 
hospitals in Thane and Zirakpur (Mohali)
• A well-defined strategic plan, backed by 
comprehensive market research and analysis by 
a dedicated team led by Sr Director – Growth 
and M &A, enables timely identification of viable 
expansion opportunities
Human Resource 
Risks• High attrition affecting the quality of care 
and service levels 
• Intense competition may result in the potential 
loss of key talent
• Risk of workplace sexual harassment• Upskilling programmes for nursing and front office 
staff to improve retention and reduce turnover
• Strengthened onboarding processes and 
training programmes. Introduction of a wellness 
and rewards portal to improve employee 
engagement and satisfaction
• Regular Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) 
awareness sessions and training to foster a safe and 
respectful work environment Particulars Risk Overview Mitigation Strategies
Operational Risks • Low patient satisfaction can potentially lead 
to loss of business
• Inconsistencies in practices and deviations from 
established care standards
• Fire hazards at healthcare facilities • Daily meetings ensure timely resolution of patient 
issues, while fortnightly reviews are conducted to 
monitor PSAT scores. The Patient Experience Teams 
gather feedback, and drive prompt service recovery,

capturing of patient feedbacks & track their closure

Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for both

Tax Strategy, Governance and 
Risk Control Framework
Max Healthcare meets its tax obligations with integrity and transparency, 
adhering to applicable regulations across all jurisdictions of operation. The 
Company’s tax practices are aligned with its broader governance principles 
and adhere to the Taxpayer’s Charter, which defines both the rights and 
responsibilities of taxpayers while promoting high standards of compliance and 
ethical conduct.
The Company has well defined tax 
strategy that captures our Tax Principles 
and acts as a guiding pillar to all 
employees of Max Healthcare, ensuring 
that their decisions made in everyday 
operations, that directly or indirectly may 
have tax implications, are aligned with the 
organisation’s tax policies. 
A robust, risk-based framework has been 
implemented to effectively identify, assess 
and manage tax risks. The Company 
ensures that all taxes are accurately 
calculated and paid on time in compliance 
with applicable laws. Max Healthcare 
responds promptly to inquiries from tax 
authorities and maintains well-organised 
documentation to support its tax positions. 
Further, transparent and accurate 
disclosure of tax-related information is 
made to stakeholders. 
The Company’s governance framework 
ensures that tax matters are managed by 
experienced & qualified professionals, 
supported by external consultants and 
advisors; whenever necessary. All tax-
related activities are conducted with 
fairness and transparency, following 
Max Healthcare’s tax principles and in 
response to evolving tax laws across its 
operational geographies. The tax function 
leverages digital and automated tools to 
enhance efficiency and accuracy. The Company has integrated a comprehensive Tax Strategy, Governance and Risk 
Control Framework into its broader corporate governance and risk management policies. 
This framework is regularly reviewed and updated internally to keep it relevant to 
evolving business needs, market conditions and regulatory changes. Our comprehensive 
tax strategy is publicly available at: 
https://max-website20-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/Max_Healthcare_Group_
Tax_Strategy_1_1ca70a5c0c.pdf
Technology Adoption Tax Risk Control
The incorporation of digital technologies 
to facilitate timely tax filings in 
accordance with statutory deadlines 
has significantly improved accuracy and 
efficiency as well as streamlined the 
Company’s overall tax reporting process.  
For indirect tax, Max Healthcare 
leverages Robotic Process Automation 
(RPA) and advanced analytical tools, 
such as GST e-invoicing and e-way 
bill software, GST Input Tax Credit 
reconciliation, GSTN validation and tools 
for drafting and filing GST returns.
For direct taxes, RPA is used to validate 
the PAN details of patients, doctors 
and vendors. Additionally, automated 
solutions have been implemented 
across the network to streamline tax 
deduction at source, generating Form-
60, eliminating manual interventions. 
At an operational level, macro-based 
templates have been deployed to bring 
efficiencies and reduce run time in 
routine compliance processes.A well-structured Tax Risk Management system is integral to identify and manage 
tax-related risks, supported by strong internal controls, defined processes and 
experienced and qualified professionals to address inherent risks associated with 
a large-scale business.

and making such

continuously complying

to assess tax regulations 
and to control various tax

Max Healthcare partnered with Credibl to transform the existing ESG reporting mechanism. This initiative directly addresses the 
challenge of gathering and validating ESG data across its large network. The Company is able to get the real-time visibility now 
in order to meet internal sustainability targets and comply with evolving regulations such as SEBI's BRSR Core framework.
The implementation of Credibl's AI-powered ESG platform enhanced data accuracy and accountability through a maker-
checker workflow and multi-level approval processes. The platform's Projects & Goals Module enabled facility-level tracking 
of sustainability efforts, while ‘AI Magic Drive’ provided automated data processing and insights. The partnership has fostered 
increased transparency and supported more informed strategic decisions on the Company’s sustainability journey.Streamlining ESG Reporting: Max Healthcare's Partnership with Credibl

As a responsible organisation, Max Healthcare conducts comprehensive materiality assessments to periodically identify the most 
significant issues impacting both its stakeholders and business operations. These insights decide strategic priorities, resource 
allocation and investment decisions. 
The Company regularly revisits and updates its material topics to ensure their relevance in light of evolving stakeholder expectations, 
regulatory changes and broader economic and industry trends. Max Healthcare conducted a materiality assessment in FY 2021–22, 
followed by a Double Materiality Assessment ("DMA") in FY 2023–24. The material topics identified in the previous reporting year 
remain the same for FY 2024-25. 
DMA plays a crucial role in enhancing 
the transparency and quality of Max 
Healthcare’s sustainability reporting 
by incorporating a balanced, dual-
perspective approach:
Impact Materiality takes an inside-
out view, evaluating the organisation’s 
influence on environmental, social and 
societal factors. For Max Healthcare, 
this includes assessing the impact of 
its operations on community health 
outcomes, environmental stewardship 
and its broader value chain, with 
particular focus on areas such as water 
and waste management. 
Financial Materiality, in contrast, adopts 
an outside-in lens, examining how 
external factors, such as governance 
practices, economic performance and

opportunities that could affect future cash

Da-Vinci Surgical Robotic System
The Da Vinci Surgical Robot is an 
advanced robotic system that enables 
surgeons to perform minimally invasive 
procedures with exceptional precision, 
dexterity and control. Using small, multi-
jointed instruments and a high-definition 
3D vision system, it provides a magnified 
view of the surgical area, aiding complex 
surgeries through smaller incisions. 
This results in less tissue damage and 
improved recovery times for patients.
Cuvis Ortho Robotic System
The Cuvis Joint Robotic System is an 
advanced surgical robotic-assisted 
system used in artificial joint replacement 
surgeries. It enables personalised pre-
surgical planning, precise cutting and with 
consistency, providing highly accurate 
results.
Versius Surgical Robotic System
The Versius Surgical Robotic System is 
a next-generation platform designed to 
enhance precision, accuracy and safety, 
offering significant advantages over 
traditional laparoscopic surgery.
ExcelsiusGPS Spine Robotic System
ExcelsiusGPS™ is the first and only 
robotic navigation platform that offers a 
comprehensive solution for both spine 
and cranial procedures. It facilitates 
repeatable and accurate trajectory 
alignment and navigation for placing 
screws, interbody implants and cranial 
instruments.
Mako Ortho Robotic System
The Mako Ortho Robotic System is a 
robotic-assisted surgical system used in 
orthopaedic procedures such as knee and 
hip replacements. It leverages a 3D model 
of the patient’s joint to assist the surgeon 
during surgery, enhancing precision 
and potentially leading to better clinical 
outcomes and quicker recovery times. 
S8 Navigation System with O-Arm
The S8 Navigation System, often 
integrated with the O-Arm imaging 
system, provides real-time, 3D navigation 
during surgical procedures. Developed 
by Medtronic, it enables surgeons to 
precisely locate anatomical structures and 
guide instruments with precision, resulting 
in more accurate and efficient surgeries. 
Max Healthcare’s hospitals are equipped with the latest medical devices and advanced tools to aid doctors in delivering accurate 
diagnostics and effective treatment plans. The Company remains committed to investing in cutting-edge medical technology and 
digital solutions to enhance patient care, build operational resilience and adapt to the evolving healthcare landscape.Cutting-edge Technology for 
Accurate Diagnosis and Treatment
Radixact X9 Tomo Therapy System
The Radixact X9 Tomotherapy is a next-
generation radiation therapy system that 
delivers highly precise, image-guided 
intensity-modulated radiation therapy 
(IMRT). Designed to target tumours 
with high-dose radiation while sparing 
surrounding healthy tissues, it features 
360-degree treatment rotation for optimal 
dose distribution and the ability to adapt 
to tumour motion.
Azurion 5 Monoplane Cath Lab Machine
Azurion 5 is a next-generation Image 
Guided Therapy System that meets 
today’s needs while supporting future 
innovations. The Azurion platform delivers 
a set of interventional tools to ensure the 
highest standards across a wide range of 
procedures. Featuring optional ClarityIQ 
technology, it offers exceptional visibility 
and high-quality output at low X-ray dose 
levels for patients of all sizes.
TruBeam STx LINAC Machine
The TrueBeam STx is an advanced 
medical linear accelerator used in 
cancer treatment, capable of targeting 
tumours even in hard-to-reach areas. It 
utilises cutting-edge imaging technology 
(ExacTrac) to visualise tumours, even 
during breathing and delivers precisely 
shaped radiation beams that conform 
to the tumour’s size and shape. This 
provides highly accurate, effective 
treatment while minimising damage to 
surrounding healthy tissues.
Azurion 7 Biplane Cathlab Machine
The Azurion 7 Series Biplane, equipped 
with two 12’’ detectors, is used for 
interventional cardiology, paediatric 
cardiology and electrophysiology. 
This advanced Image Guided Therapy 
System streamlines procedures with a 
consistent user experience, enhancing lab 
performance and offering superior patient 
care. By allowing seamless control of 
relevant applications from a single touch 
screen at the table side, the equipment 
empowers doctors to make fast, informed 
decisions within the sterile field.
Edge LINAC Machine with SGRT
The Varian Edge LINAC is a highly precise 
radiosurgery system that can be used 
with Surface Guided Radiation Therapy 
(SGRT). It features real-time tumour 
tracking, precise dose delivery and 
enhanced imaging capabilities, making it 
ideal for treating various types of tumours, 
including those in the brain, spine and 
other critical areas. 
Artis ZEE Biplane Cathlab Machine
The Artis ZEE Biplane Cathlab from 
Siemens Healthineers is a cutting-edge 
biplane angiography system featuring two 
C-arms that provide simultaneous imaging 
from two planes. This dual-place capability 
helps reduce radiation exposure and 
contrast dye usage compared to single-
plane angiography. It is widely used in 
interventional cardiology, neurology and 
vascular procedures.

Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal 
Chemotherapy System (HIPEC)
Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal 
Chemotherapy (HIPEC) is an 
advanced cancer treatment 
that involves circulating 
heated chemotherapy drugs 
within the abdominal cavity. 
Typically performed following 
cytoreductive surgery, which 
removes visible tumours, 
HIPEC targets any remaining 
cancer cells. The heated 
chemotherapy solution is 
delivered directly into the 
abdomen, effectively killing 
cancer cells and reducing the 
risk of recurrence. 
Symbia Evo Excel Dual Head 
Gamma Camera
The Siemens Symbia Evo 
Excel is a dual-head Single-
Photon Emission Computed 
Tomography (SPECT) 
gamma camera designed for 
nuclear medicine imaging. 
It features high-definition 
detector technology, a 
smaller footprint compared 
to other SPECT systems and 
improved patient comfort. 
3T Magnetom Lumina MRI 
Machine
MAGNETOM Lumina is the 
new 3T Open Bore MRI system 
that delivers unmatched 
productivity, reproducibility 
and patient satisfaction. 
Powered by advanced MR 
technology, it combines 
BioMatrix technology, the 
new Syngo MR XA software 
platform and the exclusive 
Turbo Suite to significantly 
improve care delivery.
Urolase SP Plus  
Thulium Laser
The Urolase SP Plus Thulium 
Fiber Laser is an advanced 
medical laser system used 
in urology to treat conditions 
such as kidney stones, 
prostate enlargement and 
tumours. Operating at a 1.94 
µm wavelength in Super 
Pulsed mode, it enables 
efficient stone fragmentation 
and removal, as well as 
precise enucleation and 
vaporisation of soft tissues. 
Intra OP  
Portable CT 
Intraoperative portable CT 
(iCT) scanners are mobile 
CT scanners used in the 
operating room to provide 
real-time, image-guided 
surgical guidance. They 
eliminate the need for 
patient transport, reduce 
the risk of complications 
and allow precise 
navigation during surgery. 
Solo FD 3D  
C-Arm
The Ziehm Solo FD is one 
of the most compact C-arms 
available, making it ideal for 
even the smallest treatment 
scenarios. Equipped with 
the latest CMOS flat-panel 
technology, it supports a 
wide range of applications. 
An optional large 31 cm x 
31 cm flat panel provides 
improved visualisation of 
larger anatomical regions, 
particularly in orthopaedic and 
vascular interventions.
3T Magnetom Vida MRI 
Machine
The MAGNETOM Vida, a 3T 
MRI scanner from Siemens 
Healthineers, is designed 
for both clinical applications 
and research. It features 
a new 3T magnet, strong 
gradient power and BioMatrix 
Technology, delivering 
superior image quality and 
workflow efficiency. 
Hera i10 Foetal Ultrasound 
Machine
The HERA i10 is a premier 
ultrasound system designed 
to deliver deeper insight 
through intuitive visualisations, 
advanced analytic features 
and seamless operation. 
Purpose-built for Obstetrics 
and Gynaecology, it reflects 
a strong commitment to 
supporting women’s health 
across all stages of life, 
continuously advancing 
possibilities in ultrasound 
diagnosis.
Biograph Trinion EP Digital PET CT
In 2024, Siemens Healthineers introduced 
the Biograph Trinion, its latest PET/CT 
scanner. The scanner’s detector is based 
on lutetium oxyortho silicate (LSO) crystal 
elements and delivers exceptional spatial 
resolution and an ultrafast time-of-flight 
performance of 239 picoseconds. This 
allows enhanced small lesion detectability 
and excellent sensitivity up to 128 cps/
kBq for faster scans with reduced patient 
radiation exposure.
Bravos Brachytherapy System
The Bravos system, introduced by 
Varian Medical Systems in October 
2018, is designed for high-dose-rate 
brachytherapy using 192Ir sources. It 
incorporates new features such as the 
Cam Scale, a device for daily quality 
assurance and system recalibration as 
well as channel length verification and 
distinct settings for rigid and flexible 
applicators. A study evaluated the 
precision and accuracy of the Bravos 
system for clinically relevant scenarios, 
using dummy sources.
Optis Mobile Optical Coherence 
Tomography
The Optis Mobile Optical Coherence 
Tomography (OCT) system from Abbott 
Cardiovascular uses near-infrared 
light to produce high-resolution, cross-
sectional images of the microstructure 
of blood vessels. It is widely used in 
cardiology during percutaneous coronary 
intervention (PCI) procedures, like 
stenting, to visualise vessels in detail and 
support informed treatment decisions. 
The OPTIS system, including its mobile 
version, is designed for seamless 
integration into angioplasty and stent 
placement workflows. 
CARTO 3D Navigation and Mapping 
System
The CARTO 3D Navigation and Mapping 
System is a cardiac electrophysiology 
technology used to generate real-time, 
three-dimensional maps of the heart. 
Utilising electromagnetic tracking, it 
accurately visualises catheter positioning 
within the heart, providing precise 
guidance during procedures such as 
catheter ablation. The system is widely 
used for the treatment of arrhythmias and 
other cardiac conditions
Moses Pulse Holmium Laser
The Moses Pulse Holmium Laser, 
specifically the Lumenis Pulse™ 120H, 
utilises a modulated optimised surgical 
energy system (MOSES) to improve the 
efficiency and safety of holmium laser 
lithotripsy. This innovative technology 
optimises laser pulse delivery by creating 
a vapour bubble through water separation, 
which directs the remaining energy 
towards the target stone. This results in 
more efficient stone fragmentation with 
minimised tissue damage. 
ExactVu Intraoperative Robotic Ultrasound 
with MR Fusion
The ExactVu intraoperative robotic 
ultrasound system with MRI fusion 
combines high-resolution micro-
ultrasound with MRI imaging to generate 
detailed 3D views of the prostate. This 
advanced technology enables urologists 
to precisely target biopsies for improved 
prostate cancer detection and diagnosis. 
Designed to integrate seamlessly into 
standard urological workflows, the 
ExactVu system provides high-resolution 
imaging to identify suspicious areas and 
guide precise biopsies.

Management
Max Healthcare is committed to upholding 
and advancing internationally recognized 
human rights across its operations and 
extended value chain. As a responsible 
healthcare provider, we ensure that every 
stakeholder, including patients, employees, 
healthcare professionals, partners,

The Company’s Human Rights Policy, 
aligned with global frameworks such as 
the UN Guiding Principles on Business 
and Human Rights and the ILO Core 
Conventions, explicitly prohibits all 
forms of discrimination, exploitation, 
abuse, and coercion.
The policy outlines key commitments 
including:
a) Zero tolerance for forced, bonded or 
compulsory labour, including any form 
of coercion or physical punishment.
b) Strict prohibition of child labour, 
supported by vendor audits, age 
verification systems and remediation 
protocols where needed.
c) Promotion of equal employment 
opportunity, irrespective of gender, 
caste, religion, disability, sexual 
orientation or any other status.

abled individuals, including

Risk Management ApproachesRobust HIRA processes have been 
implemented across the company’s 
operations to identify, assess and manage 
potential risks. All employees and workers 
are encouraged and trained to recognise 
and report workplace hazards and near-

formal 48-hour incident reporting process, 
which includes root cause analysis and 
mitigation plans, is deployed to address 
these issues. The progress on mitigation 
is monitored centrally for accountability 
and timely resolution.
The company has established a structured 
approach to manage risks encompassing 
assessment, mitigation, protecting

A first-of-its-kind Nursing Mobile App
Recognising the vital role nurses play 
in patient safety and delivering service 
excellence, a first-of-its-kind Nursing 
Mobile App was introduced in 
FY 2024–25. Designed to improve 
workflow efficiencies, streamline critical 
tasks, and improve overall patient 
outcomes, the app allows nurses to scan 
a patient’s unique barcode at the bedside 
and enter clinical information directly 
into their mobile devices. This improves 
data accuracy, reduces the risk of manual 
errors, and enhances patient safety. The 
app simplifies documentation by allowing 
data entry at the point of care and allows 
nurses to dedicate more time to patient 
interaction and less to paperwork. 
The app has already shown significant 
benefits—enhancing patient engagement, 
streamlining nursing workflows, reducing 
documentation errors, and improving 
bedside care delivery. Usage data from 
across Max Healthcare facilities indicate 
strong adoption, especially in the 
hospitals in Gurgaon and Shalimar Bagh, 
Delhi, where the key modules are widely 
utilised.
Looking ahead to FY 2025–26, further 
enhancements are planned. These 
include the addition of cleaning and 
disinfection checklists, infection control 
protocols, digital nursing register 
functionality, and access to an e-learning 
library. These upgrades will continue to 
support safety, compliance, and ongoing 
professional development in nursing 
practice.

The Office of Research conducted the 
world’s first human clinical trial of the 
BMR-5000 Robotic Surgery System, 
developed by Borns Medical Robotics 
Inc. The trial tested the system’s 
effectiveness in delivering minimally 
invasive procedures with greater 
control, reduced trauma and improved 
outcomes. Conducted at Max Hospital 
Vaishali, under the leadership of Dr 
Vivek Bindal and in collaboration with 
Maulana Azad Medical College, this 
landmark study evaluated the system’s 
ability to address key limitations of 
conventional endoscopic surgery, 
such as restricted movement, reversed 
controls and tremor amplification. 
The trial demonstrated the potential 
of robotic precision in real-world 
clinical settings, marking a significant 
advancement in surgical care.Trial Findings 
• No unplanned conversions to 
laparoscopic or open surgery
• Enhanced surgical 
control through up to five 
modular robotic arms
• Reduced bleeding, smaller 
incisions and less post-
operative pain for patients
• Shorter recovery and 
hospitalisation times
Following the success of this  
ground-breaking study, the Office of 
Research plans to expand its efforts 
in robotic-assisted surgery across

precision-based, patient-centred care.Hosting the World’s First Human Clinical Trial of

By 2050, nearly one in five people 
in low and middle-income countries 
will be over 60 years old, potentially 
driving a significant rise in dementia 
cases. With 35.6 million individuals 
currently affected worldwide and 7.7 
million new cases emerging each year, 
there is an urgent need to improve 
early diagnostic methods for dementia. 
This will be critical not only for effective 
treatment but also for reducing the 
emotional and financial burden on both 
patients and caregivers.
The Office of Research is developing 
advanced neuroimaging-based 
diagnostic tools tailored to the 
Indian population, aiming to create 
population-specific models for the 
early detection of dementia and 
personalised intervention strategies. 
These models integrate multimodal 
imaging, artificial intelligence and 
biomarker analysis to enable more 
accurate, precision-led diagnoses. 
By leveraging deep learning and ensemble machine learning 
techniques, the research framework 
extracts meaningful insights from 
complex data, enhancing diagnostic 
accuracy, monitoring disease 
progression and predicting cognitive 
decline with greater effectiveness.
This research builds on foundational 
work already undertaken at Max 
Healthcare, including a 12-month 
observational study titled ‘Differential 
Diagnosis Using Multimodal 
Neuroimaging’, conducted in 
partnership with Indian startup 
Brainsight AI and funded by BIRAC. 
In parallel, a ‘Normative Brain 
Morphometry’ and ‘Brain Age 
Prediction’ study is underway at Max 
Super Specialty Hospital, Saket, 
supported by the Sunita Sanghi Centre 
for Aging and Neurodegenerative 
Diseases. The ultimate goal is to 
integrate these innovations into routine 
clinical workflows, making advanced 
neuroimaging assessments more 
accessible and clinically relevant.Improving Dementia Diagnosis through 
Precision Neuroimaging

Key Digital Initiatives: FY 2024-25
Superior Patient Experiences Powered by Digitalisation 
Max Healthcare is transforming the patient experience, from pre-admission to post-discharge, through smart, scalable and responsive 
digital solutions that streamline every interaction, making care more seamless, efficient and patient-centred.
Pre-Visit 
  Max Healthcare Mobile App
Digital Immigration Tool 
The Company has introduced a digital 
immigration portal to streamline health 
screenings for visa applicants. The web-
based platform enhances convenience, 
minimises the need for in-person 
visits and improves the efficiency and 
accuracy of the process.Request for Appointment: Simplifying Appointment Booking
Max Healthcare’s mobile app now 
features a digital Request for Appointment 
(RFA) system that allows patients to 
request appointments directly, reducing 
dependence on call centres. Appointment 
requests are pushed in real-time to the 
Doctor App, where doctors can approve, 
reject or suggest walk-ins. The feature 
seamlessly integrates both virtual and in-
person consultations and allows patients 
to request Max@Home services. 
Before RFA, patients struggled to book 
appointments with high-demand or fully 
booked doctors due to unavailable slots 
and limited visibility, often resulting in 
delays or missed opportunities. Doctors 
had no insight into these unmet requests, 
while manual coordination led to longer 
average handling time (AHT) for call 
centres and a fragmented, frustrating 
experience for patients.The RFA solution has digitalised the 
entire appointment lifecycle. Patients 
now access a smart pop-up interface 
with auto-filled details and real-time 
status updates. On the doctor side, a 
dedicated ‘Appointment Requests’ tab 
classifies requests into Pending, Booked 
or Denied, supported by in-app alerts 
and logic-driven reminders. Doctors can 
respond directly, improving engagement 
and efficiency. The system also uses 
Salesforce analytics to track outcomes, 
automates the closure of stale requests 
after 7 days and reconciles appointments 
across channels to ensure data accuracy.
Since its launch, the platform has 
processed over 8,500 RFAs, resulting 
in 1,500+ confirmed bookings and 
400+ walk-in recommendations, 
significantly reducing lost demand and 
enhancing patient access.15 Lakh
Downloads
15%
of all appointment bookings 
in FY 2024-25Accounted for

IP EMR integration with Max 
doctor mobile app The Max Healthcare app consolidates 
patient records by merging profiles 
without altering the Hospital Information 
System (HIS). This helps clinicians to have 
access to complete patient histories, 
minimising errors and enabling more 
informed, efficient consultations.
The Company has implemented a 
centralised Operation Theatre (OT) 
Scheduler that guarantees seamless, 
real-time booking through a unified

and inconsistent follow-ups. This led 
to incomplete data, poor outreach 
and limited visibility into recovery

insights needed to identify outcome gaps 
across hospitals, units or individual care Max Healthcare continues to embed

procedures with the hiring of new senior

network, including 26 robotic systems.

Responding to Climate Change 
Over the years, climate change has emerged as a growing challenge for the healthcare sector, impacting both the environment 
and long-term public health. Max Healthcare recognises this risk and has taken measured steps to reduce its carbon footprint and 
strengthen climate resilience across its operations. The Company’s approach focuses on practical actions that promote resource 
efficiency, promote the use of renewable energy, prevent pollution, and drive continuous improvement.
Energy and water 
consumption across hospital 
facilities account for a 
significant portion of Max 
Healthcare’s environmental 
footprint. In response, 
energy-efficient technologies 
have been adopted, 
water-saving measures 
implemented, and renewable 
energy sources introduced 
wherever feasible. Making strategic investments 
in cleaner technologies, 
adopting lower-emission 
fuels, better waste 
management, and promoting 
environmentally responsible 
staff behaviour helps reduce 
and prevent air and soil 
pollution. Our priorities 
include handling biomedical 
waste safely and in 
compliance with regulations, 
reducing plastic use, and 
increasing recycling.Undertaking steps to offset 
the carbon footprint by 
increasing green cover both 
onsite and in surrounding 
communities. We undertake 
tree plantation drives and 
distribute solar panels to civic 
bodies, including Municipal 
Corporations, to reduce 
ambient emissions.Location-specific 
environmental indicators are 
regularly tracked to monitor 
performance and highlight 
opportunities to better 
embed sustainability into

climate-conscious model of

Climate Risk Assessment 
Max Healthcare has received 
ISO 14001:2015 certification- an 
internationally recognised standard 
for Environmental Management 
Systems—across twelve@ hospitals.

• Max Super Speciality Hospital,

• Max Super Speciality Hospital,

• Max Super Speciality Hospital,

@Represents Max Network Hospitals NumbersIn the healthcare sector, identifying 
climate related risks and opportunities 
is essential to ensuring continuity of 
care, safeguarding patient health, and 
maintaining the integrity of critical 
infrastructure. Hospitals and healthcare 
networks are uniquely vulnerable to 
both acute and chronic climate hazards 
a concern echoed by the World Health 
Organization at COP28 (Dec 2023), 
which stated that “the climate crisis is a 
health crisis.” Extreme heat, floods, water 
scarcity, and the spread of vector borne 
diseases such as dengue and malaria 
pose growing risks to public health, 
disproportionately impacting vulnerable 
groups including the elderly, children, 
and those with chronic conditions. These 
climate stressors also place pressure on 
emergency preparedness systems and 
medical supply chains, with implications 
for patient outcomes and facility 
operations.
In parallel, exposure to transition risks 
including carbon pricing, energy price 
volatility, stakeholder expectations on 
decarbonisation, and non-compliance in 
healthcare waste management was also 
evaluated. These risks are increasingly 
shaped by evolving regulatory frameworks 
such as the SEBI BRSR Core, Biomedical 
Waste Management Rules (2016, 
amended 2022), and proposed carbon 
market mechanisms under the Indian Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 
2022. Together, physical and transition 
risks represent a significant threat to 
infrastructure resilience, operational 
continuity, and the health and well-being 
of patients and employees. Understanding 
these risks enables proactive planning, 
enhances adaptive capacity, and supports 
long-term sustainability in healthcare 
service delivery.
In line with the TCFD and IFRS S2 
recommendations, Max Healthcare 
undertook a structured vulnerability 
assessment to evaluate climate exposure 
across both group-level and network-
level assets. The assessment began with 
benchmarking climate related risks and 
opportunities across the healthcare sector 
to understand emerging best practices 
and sectoral exposures. Following this, 
Max Healthcare assessed the vulnerability 
of its assets to a range of climate hazards. 
The World Bank’s ThinkHazard! platform 
was used to determine the potential 
occurrence of seven key natural hazards 
including river flooding, urban flooding, 
cyclones, landslides, extreme heat, 
water scarcity, and earthquakes in the 
regions where our facilities are located. 
These insights form the foundation of 
our physical climate risk management 
strategy and support future planning 
for infrastructure resilience, emergency 
response readiness, and operational 
continuity.

Looking ahead, Max Healthcare will undertake a comprehensive climate risk assessment employing scenario analysis. We will model 
impacts under two distinct futures a Business-as-Usual scenario (SSP 5- RCP 8.5) and an Optimistic, lower-emissions scenario (SSP 
1-RCP 2.5) to quantify the projected effects of physical and transitional climate risks on our operations, infrastructure, patient care 
delivery, and workforce resilience. This dual scenario framework aligns with leading practice and will inform our strategic investment 
decisions, resource allocation, and resilience planning. For more information, please refer to the Sustainability and Climate Change 
Policy at the website of the Company at https://www.maxhealthcare.in/investors/corporategovernance/policies-and-other-documentsMax Healthcare is modernising its 
infrastructure with advanced energy-
saving systems and optimising space 
usage across its facilities to better 
manage energy consumption, improve 
efficiency, and lower energy use per 
occupied bed days. Regular energy 
audits and continuous monitoring help 
assess environmental impact and identify 
areas for improvement.Energy-Efficient Technology
Across Max Healthcare’s network, 
traditional lighting is being replaced 
with LED fixtures, while electronically 
commutated (EC) fans and Variable 
Frequency Devices (VFDs) are used to 
optimise energy use in Heating Ventilation 
and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems. Max 
Healthcare has installed heat recovery 
pumps across its facilities as part of its 
efforts to reduce energy waste. These 
systems capture and reuse heat from 
processes such as HVAC and water 
heating, which would otherwise be lost, 
thereby improving energy efficiency and 
reducing environmental impact.Energy Efficiency 
Optimising Energy Use
Max Healthcare observed 
the ‘Greatest Hour on 
Earth’ in March 2025 
by switching off lights 
and power in non-
critical areas across its 
hospitals, reinforcing 
its commitment to 
environmental awareness.
Max Super Speciality Hospital, Vaishali, 
introduced an energy-efficient hot 
water generation system in 2024 as 
part of its ongoing efforts to improve 
operational efficiency and reduce 
environmental impact. The hospital had 
previously relied on aA combination 
of PNG-based hot water generators 
for Towers 1 and 2 and electric 
heating systems for air handling unit 
(AHU) reheating and space heating. 
These systems consumed large 
amounts of energy and incurred high 
operational costs.
The installed heat pump-based system 
uses a refrigeration cycle to provide

in creating healthier environments for

Max Healthcare undertook a large-

technique, a method for developing 
dense, native forests in a short 
period. The initiative formed part 
of its Corporate Environmental 
Responsibility (CER) programme. 
The site, impacted by urban 
development, has experienced a 
sharp decline in vegetation and 
ecological balance. Max Healthcare’s 
afforestation initiative aimed to 
increase green cover and address 
environmental concerns such as 
soil erosion, poor air quality, and 
declining groundwater levels. A total 
of 10,000 native trees were planted 
across fifteen sites, contributing to the 
creation of a natural carbon sink.

in environmental conservation.

Management Discussion and Analysis
Company Overview
Max Healthcare is a leading healthcare provider in India, committed 
to the highest standards of clinical excellence and patient care. 
Our integrated healthcare ecosystem is seamlessly supported by 
latest technology and driven by cutting-edge research, enabling 
us to deliver advanced and compassionate care across diverse 
medical disciplines.
As of March 31, 2025, our Network comprised of 22 healthcare 
facilities with a total capacity of over 5,100 beds, including more 
than 1,100 beds added during the year, primarily across Dwarka, 
Noida, Bulandshahr, and Lucknow. Our Network includes hospitals 
and medical centres owned and operated by our Company and 
its subsidiaries, as well as managed healthcare facilities and 
partner healthcare facilities (“PHFs”). Our facilities in Saket (three 
hospitals), Patparganj, Vaishali, Rajendra Place, Shalimar Bagh, 
Dwarka and Noida in Delhi NCR, along with hospitals in Mumbai, 
Mohali, Bathinda, Dehradun, Lucknow and Nagpur, serve as 
advanced tertiary and quaternary care centres, designed to deliver 
high-quality care through state-of-the-art medical technology and 
patient-centric clinical practices.Our clinical offerings are defined by expertise in tertiary and 
quaternary care, with advanced specialities such as oncology, 
cardiac sciences, neurosciences, orthopaedics, renal sciences 
and organ transplants. Our hospitals are equipped with cutting-
edge technology, including the Da Vinci and Versius surgical 
robots, LINAC Edge, 3.0T wide-bore MRI, digital PET CT and Tomo 
Therapy systems, enabling advanced treatment protocols.
In addition to our hospitals, we operate complementary businesses 
that extend our reach beyond traditional care settings. Max 
Labs, our diagnostics division, provides high-quality pathology 
and diagnostic services to patients both within and outside our 
Network, ensuring accessible and reliable testing across a wide 
geographic footprint. Max@Home, our dedicated homecare 
division, provides a comprehensive range of health and wellness 
services directly at patients’ residences, ensuring seamless care 
in the comfort of their homes.
For more details, refer ‘Max Healthcare at a Glance’ section on 
page 12 of this report. 
Indian Healthcare Industry
The global economy remained resilient in CY 24, growing by an 
estimated 3.3% despite geopolitical tensions, supply disruptions 
and trade conflicts.1 Amid this challenging backdrop, India 
maintained its strong momentum, recording a growth rate of 6.5% 
in FY 25, as per NSO’s Second Advance Estimates of GDP, and 
reaffirming its position as the fastest-growing major economy.2 
Building on this momentum of steady economic growth, the Indian 
healthcare sector is transitioning from unorganised, fragmented 
service delivery towards more structured institutional care. Within 
this sector, hospitals remain the largest and most critical segment.        
The healthcare delivery market grew from C3.9 trillion in FY 19 to  
C6.3 trillion in FY 24 and it is expected to grow at a CAGR of 
approximately 10-12% to reach C9.4-9.8 trillion in FY 28P.2
The growth is being fueled by an increasing burden of non-
communicable diseases (NCDs), ageing population, greater 
health awareness, higher per capita income and rising demand 
for tertiary and quaternary care services. Private hospitals will 
continue to witness growth, with their share of treatments (in value 
terms) expected to rise from 64% in FY 19 to around 69% by FY 28.2

Hospitals in India continue to face a significant infrastructure gap. The country’s hospital bed density stands at just 15 beds per 10,000 
people, well below the global average of 33 beds per 10,000 people, and also behind other developing countries such as Vietnam (26 
beds), Brazil (25 beds) and Malaysia (20 beds) . Based on the current bed-to-population ratio, India requires an estimated 2.4 million 
additional beds to bridge this gap.
Key Trends & Growth Drivers
Expansion of health insurance
The demand for affordable and quality healthcare is driving the steady expansion of health insurance coverage in India, supported by 
both government schemes and private sector participation. According to the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India 
(IRDAI), nearly 573 million people were covered under health insurance in FY 24, a significant increase from 288 million in FY 15. Despite 
this robust growth, overall insurance penetration remains modest at approximately 40-42% as of FY24.2
As insurance coverage becomes more widespread, there is a clear shift away from out-of-pocket healthcare spending, leading to more 
consistent revenue flows and higher capacity utilisation for organised healthcare providers. 500+

The Indian hospital sector is poised for sustained growth, fuelled 
by increasing demand for specialised healthcare services, a 
growing emphasis on tertiary and quaternary care, and ongoing 
investments in infrastructure and medical talent. As organised 
players expand their operations and refine their service 
delivery models, the industry is expected to experience greater 
consolidation, improved operational efficiencies, and broader

Opportunities and Threats
Opportunities
We are strategically positioned to capitalise on India’s evolving 
healthcare landscape with a robust pipeline of growth initiatives, 
seamless integration of acquisitions, and a relentless focus on 
operational excellence.
Accelerated capacity expansion
Robust demand for high-quality healthcare is fuelling the next 
phase of our Network expansion. Over the next 12 to 18 months, 
we are set to commission several brownfield additions – 268 
beds at Nanavati-Max, 155 beds at Max Mohali, and 400 beds 
at Max Smart (PHF). We are also adding 500 greenfield beds 
at Max Gurgaon.
During the year, we announced three transactions focused on  
asset-light, built-to-suit arrangements - a  400-bed hospital facility 
in Mohali (Zirakpur), a 500-bed facility in Thane, and a 200-bed 
facility in Pitampura. All these projects are structured to maximise Return on Capital 
Employed (ROCE) with minimal upfront investment. Following 
the success of Max Dwarka, which achieved PBIDT breakeven 
within six months, the asset-light model is now an important 
pillar of our growth strategy. This model enables rapid scale-up 
while mitigating development risks, as the project cost and time  
overruns are largely borne by the developer.
Recent acquisitions in Lucknow, Nagpur and Noida have further 
bolstered our expansion pipeline, with identified brownfield 
potential across all three locations. 
Currently, we have projects under implementation that are 
expected to add approximately 3,900 beds to our Network in the 
next three to four years, including planned capacity enhancements 
at select partner healthcare facilities.
Strategic acquisitions   
Inorganic growth continues to be a key component of our 
strategic growth initiatives. The integration and revitalisation 
of our recent acquisitions in Lucknow, Nagpur and Noida have 
significantly expanded our Network while contributing to improved 
revenue and profitability. These hospitals have demonstrated 
exemplary financial and operational performance improvement 
after acquisition.
Our approach, focused on rapid infrastructure enhancement, 
introduction of advanced clinical programmes and onboarding of 
high-calibre medical talent, has played a vital role in improving 
operational metrics such as occupancy, average revenue per 
occupied bed (ARPOB) and PBIDT per bed. We continue to 
evaluate a robust pipeline of acquisition opportunities in high-
potential markets and remain well-positioned to capitalise on 
these opportunities.

India has rapidly emerged as one of the leading destinations for medical tourism, driven by a combination of factors that uniquely 
position the country as a global healthcare hub. The nation boasts a robust and growing healthcare ecosystem, supported by advanced 
infrastructure, a large pool of highly skilled medical professionals, and cutting-edge technology. Cost-effective treatment options, often 
at a fraction of the prices charged in developed countries, attract a significant number of international patients seeking high-quality yet 
affordable care. The government’s proactive policies, streamlined visa procedures for medical travellers, and investments in healthcare 
infrastructure further enhance India’s competitiveness in this space.

Shift towards high-acuity and specialised care
The rising prevalence of non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including cancers, cardiovascular conditions, and neurological disorders, 
is driving increased demand for tertiary and quaternary care services. According to projections by the World Health Organization (WHO), 
NCDs are expected to account for approximately 72% of all global deaths by 2030, highlighting the urgent need for advanced, specialised 
healthcare infrastructure and expertise.
Rise of digitally enabled and data-driven healthcare
Healthcare delivery is rapidly evolving through the integration of technology-driven solutions, including AI-powered diagnostics, robotic-
assisted surgeries, and comprehensive Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, enhancing precision, efficiency, and patient outcomes.
Growth in outpatient and home-based care models
The rising demand for convenience, chronic care management and post-discharge recovery is accelerating the adoption of day-care 
surgeries, home ICU set-ups, physiotherapy and on-site medical room services, enabling more patient-centric and accessible care delivery.

emerged as a key revenue contributor at our flagship hospitals 
and we are actively extending this successful model to recently 
acquired facilities. The commissioning of new infrastructure, 
coupled with the deployment of advanced technologies, including 
radiation oncology units, is expected to significantly increase the 
adoption of oncology and other complex services. 
This shift is expected to further enhance key performance

Our emphasis on protocol-based care, clinical research and 
medical innovation, combined with the onboarding of top-tier 
medical talent, is showcasing our leadership in delivering complex 
tertiary and quaternary procedures.
Scaling diagnostics and home healthcare
India’s home healthcare sector is entering a high-growth phase, 
projected to surpass $ 21.3 billion by 2027, fuelled by an ageing 
population, growing chronic disease burden and a shift toward 
more accessible, patient-centric care.4 Max@Home is well-
positioned at the forefront of this shift. 
Max@Home has established itself as a frontrunner in delivering 
comprehensive, tech-enabled care outside the traditional hospital 
settings. The platform now provides a broad range of specialised 
services across multiple cities, including long-term care, chronic 
disease management, occupational health and post-acute 
services. A significant portion of the revenue is derived from repeat 
users, underscoring high patient trust and satisfaction levels. 
The diagnostics industry is poised to grow at a CAGR of 10-12% 
over FY 24 and FY 28 to H 1,275-1,375 billion led by rising literacy 
rates and disposable income among the population, leading to 
increased awareness and demand for quality healthcare services, 
including diagnostics. Organised diagnostic players are expected 
to grow at a faster rate than the overall industry between 
FY 24 and FY 28.5
Max Lab, our diagnostics platform, has extended its presence 
across multiple cities, supported by a strong network of collection 
centres and strategic partnerships. This growth has allowed us to 
deliver quality pathology and specialised testing services at scale. 
Effective utilisation of digital platforms has enabled us to capture 
a larger share of the organised diagnostics market, even as the 
sector remains highly fragmented.
Looking ahead, we remain committed to scaling these platforms 
and offerings through continued investments in technology, 
strategic partnerships and robust quality assurance initiatives.
Medical value travel and international patient services
We continue to be a preferred destination for medical tourism. 
Despite temporary headwinds in certain source countries, this 
segment has maintained strong growth momentum, reporting a 
21% year-on-year revenue increase in FY 2024-25. International 
patients now represent a meaningful portion of our occupancy and 
revenue mix, with notably higher average revenue per occupied 
bed (ARPOB) compared to the overall Network. Our strategic 
presence across multiple countries, through both Company-operated and partner offices, combined with focused outreach 
and collaborations, is driving consistent growth in this segment.
Optimising payor mix
We are strategically optimising our payor mix to maximise 
occupancy and profitability as we scale up new hospital capacities. 
In the initial stages of operations, institutional business, including 
government health schemes, plays a critical role in driving high 
bed utilisation. As our facilities reach operational maturity, we 
progressively shift towards a more favourable payor mix, with a 
focus on self-pay, insurance-backed, and international patient 
segments. Our experience across our matured hospitals validates 
the effectiveness of this phased approach in delivering sustainable 
growth in both volumes and margins.
Threats
Regulatory and pricing risks
The Indian healthcare sector operates within a dynamic regulatory 
environment, with ongoing developments in pricing, accreditation 
and compliance frameworks. Potential expansion of price caps 
by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) on 
surgical procedures, consumables and diagnostics poses a 
risk to revenue realisation. The implementation of new clinical 
protocols or mandatory accreditation requirements may lead to 
higher compliance-related expenditures. Unpredictable policy 
shifts related to government health insurance schemes, such as 
PMJAY, could affect reimbursement timelines and tariff viability for 
private hospitals.
We continue to prioritize proactive engagement with regulatory 
bodies by actively participating in key industry platforms such as 
NATHEALTH, FICCI and AHPI, ensuring effective representation of 
our sector in policy discussions.
Competitive intensity
The Indian healthcare sector is experiencing heightened 
competition in high-growth micro-markets such as Noida, 
Lucknow and Mumbai, where several leading hospital chains 
are actively expanding capacity. This intensifies competition for 
patients and clinicians while placing pressure on pricing, service 
differentiation and marketing costs. In select metropolitan micro-
markets, the pace of capacity addition may temporarily outpace 
demand, resulting in potential under-utilisation risks. 
We remain committed to sustaining our leadership by investing 
in brand equity, talent acquisition, and the skill development of 
clinical and paramedical teams, while maintaining a steadfast 
focus on service excellence, superior clinical outcomes, and 
healthcare innovation.
Shortage of skilled healthcare professionals
The healthcare sector continues to grapple with a systemic 
shortage of skilled doctors, nurses and allied health professionals. 
Elevated patient-to-clinician ratios, coupled with increasing 
procedural complexity, make the attraction and retention of high-
quality talent a critical priority. This challenge is further amplified 
4Medical Buyer- India’s Home Healthcare Market
5CRISIL Report - Assessment of the Diagnostics Industry in India (October 2024)as we expand into non-metro tier-1 cities, where the availability of 
trained medical professionals is relatively limited.
We have historically succeeded in attracting top-tier clinicians, 
especially in regions like Lucknow and Nagpur, which benefit from 
a well-established medical education ecosystem, but the risk of 
talent shortages or escalating recruitment and retention costs 
remains as the industry continues to scale.
To build a strong internal talent pipeline, we offer several structured 
medical education programmes, including DNB courses for 
medical graduates, which ensure a steady stream of well-trained, 
high-quality clinical professionals for our Network hospitals.
Integration and ramp-up risk from acquisitions
The rapid pace of our expansion, through brownfield, greenfield 
and asset-light projects, introduces execution and ramp-up 
risks inherent to new facility launches. Newly commissioned 
hospitals require considerable upfront spend towards clinical 
staffing, physician onboarding and market development initiatives 
before achieving optimal occupancy and revenue stabilisation. 
Delays in empanelment with insurance providers and third-party administrators (TPAs), or in securing clinical accreditations, 
can adversely impact the ramp-up and prolong the period of 
operating losses.
However, ramp-up risk is meaningfully mitigated in our case, 
as a large portion of our expansion is brownfield in nature, and 
several greenfield projects are in cities where we already have an 
established presence.
Delays in reimbursement and institutional payments
The increasing share of insurance patients and institutional 
payors has enhanced affordability and access for patients but 
also presents working capital challenges for our Company. 
Reimbursement delays, claim denials and procedural audits by 
insurers and regulatory bodies can affect cash flows and strain 
liquidity. The complexity of billing systems and documentation 
requirements increases the risk of disputes and revenue leakage. 
At Max Healthcare, we have established robust revenue cycle 
management practices and allocated adequate resources to 
ensure timely collections and, more importantly, to minimise 
payor-related deductions
Financial Performance and Results
During the FY 2024-25, we achieved significant milestones in both financial and operational performance. We maintained our industry 
leadership across key performance metrics and demonstrated consistent improvement throughout the year, including strong progress at our 
newly acquired hospitals in Nagpur and Lucknow. Notably, Max Dwarka achieved PBIDT breakeven within a record six months of operations. 
Across our existing Network, we continued to deliver growth in both patient volumes and average revenue per occupied bed (ARPOB).

Our Company has implemented a robust, well-integrated internal 
control framework supported by advanced IT systems and 
workflow-enabled processes. The controls are continuously 
reviewed and enhanced through periodic risk control assessments 
and testing. A comprehensive suite of policies, standard operating 
procedures (SOPs), and guidelines govern all business functions. 
These are regularly updated and are accessible to relevant 
employees via a centralized digital platform, ensuring transparency 
and consistency across the organization. The framework is 
designed to ensure accuracy in financial reporting, safeguard 
assets and support effective decision-making. Our Internal Audit 
Plan remains dynamic and aligned with strategic risks, and audit 
findings are closely monitored by the Audit Committee.
During the reporting period, the internal controls were assessed 
and no material weaknesses in design or execution were 
identified. The statutory auditors did not report any material 
weaknesses or mis-statements arising from control deficiencies in 
the course of their audit.
